title: Ethical Hacking Fundamentals & Baseline Recording
learningObjectives: Identify the operating system release, kernel architecture, and hostname
Inspect network interface addresses, subnet masks, and default gateways
Record baseline hardware and system parameters into an audit inventory
Generate an authorized, compliant technical lab assessment report
prerequisites: Basic command line navigation and understanding of IP addressing.
requiredSoftware: Linux Bash terminal (or safe simulator), iproute2, uname, hostnamectl.
setupInstructions: Ensure you are operating within the isolated training enclave. Open the interactive terminal simulator below to begin executing commands against the authorized local stack.

steps.title: Audit Operating System Release and Kernel Architecture
steps.command: uname -a; cat /etc/os-release | grep -E '^(NAME|VERSION)='
steps.explanation: Executes 'uname -a' to print kernel release, machine architecture, and hostname. Pipes '/etc/os-release' into grep to cleanly extract the distribution name and version.
steps.expectedOutput:
Linux cadet-node 5.15.0-89-generic #99-Ubuntu SMP Mon Oct 16 14:10:00 UTC 2026 x86_64
NAME="Ubuntu"
VERSION="22.04.3 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)"
steps.interpretation: Confirms the host is running a 64-bit Linux kernel on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. Establishing the exact OS kernel is vital during penetration tests to identify kernel-specific privileges and patching levels.

steps.title: Inspect Network Interfaces and Routing Configuration
steps.command: ip -br addr show; ip route show
steps.explanation: Uses 'ip -br addr show' to print a brief summary of all physical and virtual network interfaces and assigned IPs, followed by the active kernel routing table.
steps.expectedOutput:
lo               UNKNOWN        127.0.0.1/8 ::1/128 
eth0             UP             10.10.20.10/24 fe80::20c:29ff:fe4a:8b9c/64 
default via 10.10.20.1 dev eth0 proto static onlink 
10.10.20.0/24 dev eth0 proto kernel scope link src 10.10.20.10
steps.interpretation: Indicates eth0 is active on subnet 10.10.20.0/24 with IP 10.10.20.10, routing default traffic through gateway 10.10.20.1. This verifies the boundaries for our authorized engagement.

steps.title: Record Test Environment Telemetry and Generate Baseline Audit
steps.command: echo "[AUDIT] Host: $(hostname) | Date: $(date -u) | Kernel: $(uname -r)" > baseline_env.txt; cat baseline_env.txt
steps.explanation: Creates a structured baseline audit record in a local text file documenting hostname, UTC timestamp, and kernel version for inclusion in the final penetration testing deliverable.
steps.expectedOutput: [AUDIT] Host: cadet-node | Date: Sat Oct 17 10:45:00 UTC 2026 | Kernel: 5.15.0-89-generic
steps.interpretation: Documenting verifiable timestamps and host metrics proves the assessment was conducted strictly within the agreed Rules of Engagement (RoE) window.

steps.title: Generate Authorized Technical Lab Assessment Report
steps.command:
cat << 'EOF' > ceh_audit_report.md
# Penetration Testing Technical Assessment Report
**Engagement**: CEH v13 Authorized Training Enclave
**Target Scope**: 10.10.20.0/24
**Tested By**: Cadet Security Analyst
**Methodology**: NIST SP 800-115 / CEH Assessment Framework
**Executive Summary**: Comprehensive baseline audit established on subnet 10.10.20.0/24. All testing strictly restricted to authorized IPs.
EOF
head -n 7 ceh_audit_report.md
steps.explanation: Creates a structured Markdown lab assessment report documenting the scope, methodology, tester identification, and executive summary in compliance with Rules of Engagement (RoE).
steps.expectedOutput:
# Penetration Testing Technical Assessment Report
**Engagement**: CEH v13 Authorized Training Enclave
**Target Scope**: 10.10.20.0/24
**Tested By**: Cadet Security Analyst
**Methodology**: NIST SP 800-115 / CEH Assessment Framework
steps.interpretation: Standardizes ethical hacking deliverables. Transparent documentation protects both the client and testing organization from scope disputes.

troubleshooting.cause: The iproute2 package may not be in system PATH on older distributions.
troubleshooting.solution: Use legacy 'ifconfig' or verify PATH environment variables.

troubleshooting.cause: Attempting to write to a root-restricted directory.
troubleshooting.solution: Ensure current working directory is within your user home directory (/home/cadet).

securityConcepts: Ethical hacking requires strict adherence to legal authorization and thorough documentation. Before initiating technical scans, an ethical hacker must define the testing scope, verify network interfaces, and record baselines so any subsequent anomalies can be accurately attributed.
defensiveRemediation: Organizations should maintain an authoritative Asset Management Inventory (CIS Control 1 & 2) tracking every system, IP address, and OS build in production. Regular audits detect rogue or unmanaged machines before attackers find them.
checklist: Identified host operating system and kernel architecture
Documented IP address and gateway boundaries on eth0
Generated baseline audit record for RoE verification
Confirmed testing is restricted to private subnet 10.10.20.0/24
Generated formal technical lab assessment report

title: DNS Enumeration and Footprinting
learningObjectives: Perform authoritative DNS lookups using dig and nslookup
Query and interpret A, MX, NS, and TXT resource records
Query registrar information safely via WHOIS
Analyze email authentication records (SPF, DMARC) for spoofing risks
prerequisites: Understanding of the Domain Name System hierarchy and client-server models.
setupInstructions: Point your DNS inquiries towards the lab DNS gateway 10.10.20.2 to query the simulated domain corp-target.local.

steps.title: Query Authoritative Name Servers and Mail Exchangers
steps.command: dig @10.10.20.2 corp-target.local NS +noall +answer; dig @10.10.20.2 corp-target.local MX +noall +answer
steps.explanation: Directs DNS queries to nameserver 10.10.20.2 requesting Name Server (NS) and Mail Exchanger (MX) records, suppressing boilerplate text with +noall +answer.
steps.expectedOutput:
corp-target.local.    3600    IN    NS    ns1.corp-target.local.
corp-target.local.    3600    IN    NS    ns2.corp-target.local.
corp-target.local.    3600    IN    MX    10 mail.corp-target.local.
steps.interpretation: Identifies that mail is processed by mail.corp-target.local with priority 10, and two DNS servers (ns1, ns2) manage the zone.

steps.title: Extract and Evaluate TXT Records for SPF Policies
steps.command: dig @10.10.20.2 corp-target.local TXT +noall +answer
steps.explanation: Queries TXT records to discover domain verification tokens, SPF configurations, and domain ownership assertions.
steps.expectedOutput:
corp-target.local.    3600    IN    TXT    "v=spf1 ip4:10.10.20.0/24 include:_spf.corp-target.local ~all"
corp-target.local.    3600    IN    TXT    "dmarc=v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:dmarc@corp-target.local"
steps.interpretation: The SPF policy specifies '~all' (SoftFail), meaning unauthorized senders are flagged but not hard-rejected. The DMARC policy is set to 'p=quarantine'.

steps.title: Attempt Authorized DNS Zone Transfer (AXFR Audit)
steps.command: dig @10.10.20.2 corp-target.local axfr
steps.explanation: Attempts a full zone transfer using the AXFR query type to determine whether the nameserver improperly allows zone transfers to arbitrary clients.
steps.expectedOutput:
;; Connection to 10.10.20.2#53: Transfer failed: REFUSED
;; AXFR record query denied by ACL 'trusted-secondaries'
steps.interpretation: The nameserver securely returns REFUSED. An insecure server would have dumped all internal hostnames, IP allocations, and sensitive staging servers.

steps.title: Attempt and Interpret DNS Zone Transfer (AXFR) Security
steps.command: dig @10.10.20.2 corp-target.local AXFR
steps.explanation: Attempts a full DNS zone transfer (AXFR) over TCP port 53. If improperly secured, AXFR dumps every host and internal IP in the entire domain hierarchy.
steps.expectedOutput:
;; Connection to 10.10.20.2#53: Transfer failed: REFUSED
;; AXFR record query denied by ACL trusted-secondaries
steps.interpretation: The zone transfer request was properly REFUSED by the DNS server. This confirms defensive hardening: zone transfers are restricted strictly to authorized secondary nameservers.

troubleshooting.issue: Connection timed out; no servers could be reached
troubleshooting.cause: DNS server IP is unreachable or firewall blocks UDP/TCP port 53.
troubleshooting.solution: Verify reachability with 'ping 10.10.20.2' and check local routing.

securityConcepts: DNS records represent an organization's public directory. Attackers use DNS queries to enumerate mail servers, subdomains, cloud services, and email authentication defenses. Restricting zone transfers (AXFR) to trusted secondary IPs prevents wholesale reconnaissance.
defensiveRemediation: Configure BIND/Named with 'allow-transfer { trusted_secondary_ips; };'. Enforce strict SPF with '-all' (HardFail) and DMARC with 'p=reject' to defeat domain spoofing.
checklist: Queried NS and MX records for target domain
Audited TXT records for SPF and DMARC policies
Verified zone transfers (AXFR) are properly restricted (REFUSED)
Documented mail gateway IPs for subsequent assessment phases
Evaluated DNS Zone Transfer (AXFR) security controls

title: Network Scanning & Service Versioning
learningObjectives: Discover live hosts on a private CIDR subnet using ARP/ICMP ping sweeps
Execute TCP SYN stealth scans (-sS) against authorized target machines
Interrogate open listening ports for daemon version identification (-sV)
Analyze response banners and OS fingerprint signatures
prerequisites: Understanding of the TCP 3-way handshake (SYN, SYN/ACK, ACK) and flags.
setupInstructions: Target host 10.10.20.50 has been provisioned with standard network services. Ensure your scan probes remain within the 10.10.20.0/24 subnet.

steps.title: Host Discovery Sweep Across Lab Subnet
steps.explanation: Executes a ping sweep (-sn) across the /24 subnet without scanning ports, identifying live hosts through ARP requests on local links.
steps.expectedOutput:
Nmap scan report for 10.10.20.1
Host is up (0.00045s latency).
Nmap scan report for 10.10.20.10
Host is up (0.00010s latency).
Nmap scan report for 10.10.20.50
Host is up (0.00082s latency).
Nmap done: 256 IP addresses (3 hosts up) scanned in 1.42 seconds
steps.interpretation: Identifies three active machines: Gateway (10.10.20.1), Cadet node (10.10.20.10), and Target server (10.10.20.50).

steps.title: TCP SYN Stealth Scan with Service Version Detection
steps.explanation: Performs a half-open TCP SYN scan (-sS) against designated ports and queries responding sockets for software banners (-sV).
steps.expectedOutput:
PORT     STATE SERVICE VERSION
21/tcp   open  ftp     vsftpd 2.3.4
22/tcp   open  ssh     OpenSSH 8.9p1 Ubuntu 3ubuntu0.4
80/tcp   open  http    Apache httpd 2.4.52 ((Ubuntu))
443/tcp  open  ssl/http Apache httpd 2.4.52
3306/tcp open  mysql   MySQL 8.0.35-0ubuntu0.22.04.1
steps.interpretation: Port 21 is running vsftpd 2.3.4 (notable for historic backdoor signatures), SSH on 22, Apache 2.4.52 on 80/443, and MySQL on 3306.

steps.title: Aggressive OS and Script Scan against Selected Ports
steps.explanation: Runs default NSE scripts (-sC) to collect HTTP title and methods, plus TCP/IP stack fingerprinting (-O) to identify the operating system.
steps.expectedOutput:
PORT    STATE SERVICE
80/tcp  open  http
|_http-title: HackRange Training Portal - Authorized Access Only
|_http-server-header: Apache/2.4.52 (Ubuntu)
443/tcp open  https
| ssl-cert: Subject: commonName=hackrange.local
Device type: general purpose
Running: Linux 5.X
OS CPE: cpe:/o:linux:linux_kernel:5
steps.interpretation: Reveals the web title, web server header, SSL commonName, and identifies the underlying kernel as Linux 5.X.

steps.title: Interpret Comprehensive Scan Results and Synthesize Attack Surface Matrix
steps.command:
cat << 'EOF' > target_surface_summary.txt
PORT    STATE SERVICE VERSION
21/tcp  open  ftp     vsftpd 2.3.4 (Vulnerable Backdoor CVE-2011-2523)
22/tcp  open  ssh     OpenSSH 8.9p1 (Audit password auth)
80/tcp  open  http    Apache 2.4.52 (Inspect security headers)
445/tcp open  smb     Samba 4.15.13 (Check null sessions)
EOF
cat target_surface_summary.txt
steps.explanation: Synthesizes port scan findings into a structured attack surface inventory, linking listening ports directly to identified service versions and potential threat vectors.
steps.expectedOutput:
PORT    STATE SERVICE VERSION
21/tcp  open  ftp     vsftpd 2.3.4 (Vulnerable Backdoor CVE-2011-2523)
22/tcp  open  ssh     OpenSSH 8.9p1 (Audit password auth)
80/tcp  open  http    Apache 2.4.52 (Inspect security headers)
445/tcp open  smb     Samba 4.15.13 (Check null sessions)
steps.interpretation: Correlating discovered services against known vulnerability databases is the essential precursor to the Exploitation and Vulnerability Analysis phases.

troubleshooting.issue: Note: Host seems down. If it is really up, but blocking our ping probes, try -Pn
troubleshooting.cause: Target firewall is dropping ICMP echo requests.
troubleshooting.solution: Append '-Pn' to bypass host discovery and scan ports directly.

securityConcepts: Port scanning maps network services by observing TCP flag behavior. Open ports respond to SYN with SYN/ACK; closed ports respond with RST/ACK; filtered ports drop packets or return ICMP unreachable. Stealth SYN scans minimize log generation on unhardened services.
defensiveRemediation: Deploy stateful firewalls to drop unsolicited incoming SYN probes on non-public ports. Implement network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) like Suricata with port-scan threshold detection.
checklist: Completed CIDR host discovery sweep
Identified open TCP services and exact daemon versions
Inspected HTTP headers and TLS certificate metadata
Logged open ports in the engagement findings repository
Synthesized attack surface matrix correlating ports to services

title: Service Enumeration & Socket Inspection
learningObjectives: Inspect listening TCP and UDP sockets with modern kernel utilities (ss)
Audit service process mappings and configuration bindings
Enumerate SMB shares and RPC endpoints using standard client commands
Document exposed services into an actionable attack tree
prerequisites: Understanding of TCP ports, daemon architectures, and socket states.
setupInstructions: Execute socket inspection on target 10.10.20.50 to audit daemon bindings and exposed network shares.

steps.title: Identify Local Listening Services and Network Sockets
steps.command: ss -tulpn
steps.explanation: Executes 'ss -tulpn' to inspect all TCP and UDP listening sockets, identifying local bind addresses (0.0.0.0 vs 127.0.0.1) and process IDs.
steps.expectedOutput:
Netid State  Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address:Port  Peer Address:Port Process
tcp   LISTEN 0      128    0.0.0.0:22          0.0.0.0:*     users:(("sshd",pid=842,fd=3))
tcp   LISTEN 0      511    0.0.0.0:80          0.0.0.0:*     users:(("apache2",pid=1024,fd=4))
tcp   LISTEN 0      128    127.0.0.1:3306      0.0.0.0:*     users:(("mysqld",pid=920,fd=21))
tcp   LISTEN 0      128    0.0.0.0:445         0.0.0.0:*     users:(("smbd",pid=1102,fd=35))
steps.interpretation: Reveals OpenSSH (22), Apache (80), and Samba (445) are exposed to all interfaces (0.0.0.0), while MySQL (3306) is properly restricted to localhost (127.0.0.1).

steps.title: Inspect Service Configurations and Daemon Bindings
steps.command: cat /etc/nginx/nginx.conf 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'listen|server_name|access_log' || echo 'listen 80 default_server; server_name corp-target.local; access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log combined;'
steps.explanation: Examines daemon configuration files to verify port bindings, virtual host definitions, and security logging settings.
steps.expectedOutput: listen 80 default_server; server_name corp-target.local; access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log combined;
steps.interpretation: Confirms the HTTP service is bound to port 80 and logs client requests in standard Apache/Nginx combined format.

steps.title: Enumerate SMB Shares and RPC Endpoints
steps.command: smbclient -L //10.10.20.50 -N; smbclient //10.10.20.50/public -N -c 'ls'
steps.explanation: Connects with an unauthenticated null session (-N) to enumerate visible SMB shares, then inspects the contents of the public share.
steps.expectedOutput:
Sharename       Type      Comment
---------       ----      -------
print$          Disk      Printer Drivers
public          Disk      Cadet Shared Training Workspace
IPC$            IPC       IPC Service (Samba Server)

  .                                   D        0  Sat Oct 17 11:20:00 2026
  ..                                  D        0  Sat Oct 17 11:20:00 2026
  confidential_policy_v2.pdf          A   104857  Sat Oct 17 11:22:00 2026
steps.interpretation: Identifies an unauthenticated share 'public' exposing 'confidential_policy_v2.pdf'. Information leakage via SMB is a frequent vector in internal corporate breaches.

steps.title: Document Exposed Services and Attack Surface Inventory Matrix
steps.command:
cat << 'EOF' > exposed_services_inventory.tsv
PORT	PROTO	SERVICE	DAEMON	VERSION	EXPOSURE
22	TCP	SSH	OpenSSH	8.9p1	Internal Mgmt
80	TCP	HTTP	Apache	2.4.52	Public Enclave
445	TCP	SMB	Samba	4.15.13	Public Share
EOF
cat exposed_services_inventory.tsv
steps.explanation: Compiles discovered service endpoints into a structured inventory matrix for technical risk evaluation.
steps.expectedOutput:
PORT	PROTO	SERVICE	DAEMON	VERSION	EXPOSURE
22	TCP	SSH	OpenSSH	8.9p1	Internal Mgmt
80	TCP	HTTP	Apache	2.4.52	Public Enclave
445	TCP	SMB	Samba	4.15.13	Public Share
steps.interpretation: Creates a structured asset record fulfilling CIS Control 2 (Inventory and Control of Software Assets).

troubleshooting.cause: Guest and anonymous browsing has been disabled on the target Samba server.
troubleshooting.solution: Supply authorized lab credentials using '-U cadet%password'.

securityConcepts: Enumeration transitions a pentest from general host discovery into detailed mapping of specific software daemons, shares, user accounts, and configuration files. Misconfigured access controls on file shares frequently yield administrative credentials.
defensiveRemediation: Disable SMBv1 entirely. Restrict SMB shares by setting 'restrict anonymous = 2' and 'map to guest = Never' in smb.conf. Audit share ACLs to ensure sensitive backups are not stored in public shares.
checklist: Audited active listening daemons and socket bindings with ss
Inspected daemon service configuration files
Enumerated SMB shares and public folders with null session
Documented exposed services inventory into technical matrix

title: Vulnerability Analysis & CVSS Prioritization
learningObjectives: Correlate discovered software versions with the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD)
Calculate CVSS v3.1 Base, Temporal, and Environmental scores
Perform simulated vulnerability scanner triage and false-positive filtering
Formulate a risk-ranked remediation action plan
prerequisites: Familiarity with CVE IDs, CVSS metrics, and software versioning schemes.
requiredSoftware: python3 / py, curl, jq (or simulated terminal).
setupInstructions: Review the service discovery outputs from Lab 03 and query vulnerability references for vsftpd 2.3.4 and Apache 2.4.52.

steps.title: Query CVE Database for Discovered vsftpd 2.3.4 Daemon
steps.command: curl -s "https://cve.circl.lu/api/cve/CVE-2011-2523" | jq '{id, cvss, summary}' || echo '{"id":"CVE-2011-2523","cvss":9.8,"summary":"vsftpd 2.3.4 contains a backdoor that opens a root shell on port 6200 when a username containing :) is supplied."}'
steps.explanation: Queries the CVE database for vulnerability details regarding the vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor vulnerability.
steps.interpretation: Identifies a critical Remote Code Execution vulnerability (CVSS 9.8) with network attack vector (AV:N) and zero privileges required (PR:N).

steps.title: Calculate CVSS v3.1 Vector String and Severity Rating
steps.command: echo "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H" | awk '{print "Vector: " $1 " | Base Score: 9.8 (CRITICAL)"}'
steps.explanation: Calculates the CVSS 3.1 Base Metrics: Network vector, Low complexity, No privileges required, No user interaction, Unchanged scope, High Confidentiality/Integrity/Availability impact.
steps.expectedOutput: Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H | Base Score: 9.8 (CRITICAL)
steps.interpretation: Confirms the finding qualifies as a Tier-1 CRITICAL emergency patch priority requiring immediate remediation.

steps.title: Generate Actionable Remediation Specification
steps.command:
echo -e "[REMEDIATION PLAN]
Target: 10.10.20.50:21
Action: Remove vsftpd 2.3.4 immediately. Deploy latest supported vsftpd (>=3.0.5) or migrate to SFTP (OpenSSH).
Verification: Confirm port 21 is closed or running hardened daemon with TLS enforced."
steps.explanation: Constructs the formal remediation advisory for systems administrators.
steps.expectedOutput:
[REMEDIATION PLAN]
Target: 10.10.20.50:21
Action: Remove vsftpd 2.3.4 immediately. Deploy latest supported vsftpd (>=3.0.5) or migrate to SFTP (OpenSSH).
Verification: Confirm port 21 is closed or running hardened daemon with TLS enforced.
steps.interpretation: Provides the system owner with explicit replacement instructions and verification criteria.

steps.title: Formulate Security Remediation Roadmap and Patching Advisory
steps.command:
cat << 'EOF' > remediation_advisory.md
# Vulnerability Remediation Advisory
1. Immediate: Decommission or upgrade vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor to vsftpd 3.0.5+.
2. Short-term: Enforce SMB signing and disable anonymous guest access on Samba.
3. Medium-term: Deploy automated vulnerability scanning and patch management lifecycle.
EOF
cat remediation_advisory.md
steps.explanation: Outlines a prioritized patch management timeline categorizing fixes by criticality (Immediate, Short-term, Medium-term).
steps.expectedOutput:
# Vulnerability Remediation Advisory
1. Immediate: Decommission or upgrade vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor to vsftpd 3.0.5+.
2. Short-term: Enforce SMB signing and disable anonymous guest access on Samba.
3. Medium-term: Deploy automated vulnerability scanning and patch management lifecycle.
steps.interpretation: Penetration testers must deliver actionable remediation steps that system administrators can operationalize immediately.

troubleshooting.issue: API rate limit reached on public CVE endpoints
troubleshooting.cause: External API request throttled.
troubleshooting.solution: The platform simulator provides immediate offline cached responses.

securityConcepts: Vulnerability analysis is not simply running a scanner; it requires validating findings, evaluating exploitability in the local context, and scoring impact accurately using CVSS v3.1 to ensure critical risks are patched before adversaries can exploit them.
defensiveRemediation: Implement continuous automated vulnerability scanning, subscribe to CISA KEV feeds, and establish a strict SLA for critical vulnerabilities (e.g., remediation within 72 hours of disclosure).
checklist: Correlated vsftpd 2.3.4 with CVE-2011-2523
Calculated CVSS v3.1 vector string and 9.8 Critical rating
Documented exploit mechanics (backdoor port 6200)
Formulated remediation plan replacing obsolete FTP with SFTP
Formulated security remediation roadmap and patch advisory

title: System Hacking & Privilege Auditing
learningObjectives: Enumerate local user accounts, groups, and shell configurations
Audit POSIX file permissions for sensitive system files (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow)
Locate insecure SUID/SGID executable binaries
Review sudo privileges and establish least-privilege configurations
prerequisites: Understanding of Linux user identifiers (UID), group identifiers (GID), and permission bits (rwx).
setupInstructions: Log into the target node as unprivileged operator 'cadet' and conduct a thorough local privilege escalation audit.

steps.title: Enumerate Current User Identity and Group Memberships
steps.command: id; whoami; cat /etc/passwd | grep -E ':(0|100[0-9]):'
steps.explanation: Prints current UID, GID, and supplementary groups. Filters /etc/passwd to show root (UID 0) and standard interactive user accounts (UID >= 1000).
steps.expectedOutput:
uid=1001(cadet) gid=1001(cadet) groups=1001(cadet),27(sudo),100(users)
cadet
root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash
cadet:x:1001:1001:Cadet Trainee:/home/cadet:/bin/bash
operator:x:1002:1002:Range Operator:/home/operator:/bin/bash
steps.interpretation: Confirms 'cadet' is an unprivileged user (UID 1001) but is currently a member of the 'sudo' group (GID 27).

steps.title: Audit SUID Executables Across the Filesystem
steps.command: find / -perm -4000 -user root -type f 2>/dev/null | grep -E '/(usr/bin|bin|usr/local)' | head -n 10
steps.explanation: Searches for root-owned files with the SUID bit set (mask -4000), discarding permission denied errors from /proc and /sys.
steps.expectedOutput:
/usr/bin/passwd
/usr/bin/sudo
/usr/bin/newgrp
/usr/bin/gpasswd
/usr/bin/chfn
/usr/bin/chsh
/usr/bin/pkexec
/usr/local/bin/custom_backup
steps.interpretation: Standard SUID binaries (passwd, sudo, pkexec) are expected, but '/usr/local/bin/custom_backup' is a non-standard custom binary that warrants reverse-engineering for privilege flaws.

steps.title: Audit Sudo Privileges and NOPASSWD Directives
steps.command: sudo -l -U cadet 2>/dev/null || echo "User cadet may run the following commands on this host: (ALL : ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/systemctl restart apache2"
steps.explanation: Lists allowed commands for user 'cadet' in the sudoers configuration.
steps.expectedOutput:
User cadet may run the following commands on this host:
    (ALL : ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/systemctl restart apache2
steps.interpretation: Cadet can restart apache2 without entering a password. If the apache configuration or service unit is writable by cadet, this presents a privilege escalation vector.

steps.title: Formulate Linux Host Hardening and Secure Configuration Recommendations
steps.command:
cat << 'EOF' > linux_hardening_guide.sh
# Linux Privilege Hardening Recommendations
# 1. Strip SUID bit from non-essential binaries:
chmod u-s /usr/local/bin/custom_backup
# 2. Enforce strict sudoers rules with password requirement:
echo 'cadet ALL=(ALL) ALL' > /etc/sudoers.d/cadet
# 3. Harden filesystem umask in /etc/profile:
umask 027
EOF
cat linux_hardening_guide.sh
steps.explanation: Generates a system hardening script addressing SUID privileges, least-privilege sudo configuration, and restrictive filesystem umasks.
steps.expectedOutput:
# Linux Privilege Hardening Recommendations
# 1. Strip SUID bit from non-essential binaries:
chmod u-s /usr/local/bin/custom_backup
# 2. Enforce strict sudoers rules with password requirement:
echo 'cadet ALL=(ALL) ALL' > /etc/sudoers.d/cadet
# 3. Harden filesystem umask in /etc/profile:
umask 027
steps.interpretation: Remediating dangerous SUID permissions prevents local privilege escalation (LPE) even if an attacker secures a low-privilege foothold.

troubleshooting.issue: find: command hangs or generates thousands of lines
troubleshooting.cause: Traversing mounted network shares or dynamic pseudo-filesystems (/proc, /sys).
troubleshooting.solution: Use '-xdev' flag to prevent find from traversing into mounted filesystems.

securityConcepts: System hacking involves gaining access, escalating privileges, executing applications, and maintaining persistence. Privilege escalation occurs when an attacker exploits system misconfigurations (such as SUID binaries or overly permissive sudoers rules) to elevate from unprivileged user to root or SYSTEM.
defensiveRemediation: Audit sudoers configurations regularly. Avoid wildcard NOPASSWD directives. Mount user-writable directories (/tmp, /home, /dev/shm) with the 'nosuid' and 'noexec' mount options to prevent unauthorized SUID binary execution.
checklist: Audited user accounts and groups in /etc/passwd
Inspected filesystem for non-standard SUID root binaries
Discovered custom_backup SUID executable in /usr/local/bin
Audited sudo permissions and documented least-privilege recommendations
Formulated Linux privilege hardening and secure config advisory

title: Static Malware Analysis & Integrity Hashing
learningObjectives: Calculate cryptographic SHA-256 hashes to establish file integrity baselines
Identify authentic file formats using magic bytes inspection (file utility)
Extract embedded ASCII and Unicode strings to uncover URLs and function names
Verify antivirus detection pipelines using the standardized EICAR test string
prerequisites: Understanding of file headers, ASCII encoding, and cryptographic hashing.
setupInstructions: Work strictly within the isolated analysis sandbox. Do not execute suspicious files during static analysis.

steps.title: Compute SHA-256 Hash and Inspect File Magic Header
steps.command: echo 'X5O!P%@AP[4\PZX54(P^)7CC)7}$EICAR-STANDARD-ANTIVIRUS-TEST-FILE!$H+H*' > eicar.com; sha256sum eicar.com; file eicar.com
steps.explanation: Generates the standardized, harmless EICAR test string, calculates its SHA-256 digest, and checks its file format using 'file'.
steps.expectedOutput:
275a021bbfb6489e54d471899f7db9d1663fc695ec2fe2a2c4538aabf651fd0f  eicar.com
eicar.com: EICAR virus test files
steps.interpretation: The SHA-256 digest matches the global known EICAR hash. Antivirus software immediately flags this hash as a positive detection test.

steps.title: Detect Disguised Executable Using Magic Bytes Analysis
steps.command: printf '\x7fELF\x02\x01\x01\x00' > invoice_report.pdf; file invoice_report.pdf
steps.explanation: Creates a simulated test file named invoice_report.pdf containing the Linux ELF executable magic byte sequence (\x7fELF) rather than PDF headers (%PDF).
steps.expectedOutput: invoice_report.pdf: ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV)
steps.interpretation: The 'file' command exposes that despite the .pdf extension, the payload is an ELF executable. Attackers frequently use double extensions to deceive users.

steps.title: Extract Embedded Strings to Uncover C2 Endpoints
steps.command:
echo -e 'Mozilla/5.0
http://c2-beacon.darknet.internal:8080/checkin
VirtualAlloc
WriteProcessMemory' > sample_dump.bin; strings -n 8 sample_dump.bin
steps.explanation: Extracts contiguous sequences of 8 or more printable characters from the sample binary dump.
steps.expectedOutput:
Mozilla/5.0
http://c2-beacon.darknet.internal:8080/checkin
VirtualAlloc
WriteProcessMemory
steps.interpretation: Reveals suspicious Windows API imports (VirtualAlloc, WriteProcessMemory used in process injection) and a command-and-control (C2) beacon URL.

steps.title: Safe Antivirus Test-File Demonstrations (EICAR Standard Test String)
steps.command: echo -n 'X5O!P%@AP[4\PZX54(P^)7CC)7}$EICAR-STANDARD-ANTIVIRUS-TEST-FILE!$H+H*' > eicar.com.txt; sha256sum eicar.com.txt
steps.explanation: Creates the industry-standard benign EICAR antivirus test file (68-byte ASCII) to verify antivirus detection without deploying real malicious code.
steps.expectedOutput: 275a021bbfb6489e54d471899f7db9d1663fc695ec2fe2a2c4538aabf651fd0f  eicar.com.txt
steps.interpretation: The computed SHA-256 matches the universal standard EICAR test string hash. This demonstrates that security tools can be safely validated in testing environments without risk.

troubleshooting.issue: strings command returns thousands of meaningless characters
troubleshooting.cause: Default minimum length is 4 characters, which captures binary noise.
troubleshooting.solution: Increase threshold with 'strings -n 10' or grep for specific patterns like 'http' or '.exe'.

securityConcepts: Static analysis inspects malware components without executing the binary. By checking cryptographic hashes, magic bytes, PE headers, and embedded strings, analysts can extract indicators of compromise (IoCs) safely in an isolated environment.
defensiveRemediation: Deploy endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions that verify file headers regardless of file extensions. Block execution of binaries from user-writable directories (%AppData%, /tmp).
checklist: Generated and verified EICAR standard antivirus test hash
Detected disguised ELF binary masked with .pdf extension
Extracted C2 beacon URL and suspicious API calls via strings
Cataloged SHA-256 IoCs into threat intelligence database
Validated safe antivirus test string (EICAR) hashing

title: Packet Sniffing & Protocol Dissection
learningObjectives: Capture network packets on local interfaces using tcpdump
Apply Berkeley Packet Filters (BPF) to isolate specific protocols
Dissect Ethernet II, IPv4, TCP, and application layer payload headers
Identify cleartext credential leakage across unencrypted protocols
prerequisites: Understanding of the OSI model, TCP/IP stack layers, and encapsulation.
setupInstructions: Start a live capture session in the terminal simulator and observe packet exchanges between the cadet workstation and local services.

steps.title: Capture Loopback Traffic and Inspect ICMP Protocol Headers
steps.command: tcpdump -i lo -c 2 -nn -v 'icmp' & sleep 0.5; ping -c 1 127.0.0.1
steps.explanation: Binds tcpdump to the loopback interface (lo) with filter 'icmp' to capture ICMP echo requests and replies, inspecting IP TTL and checksum headers.
steps.expectedOutput:
IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 58921, offset 0, flags [DF], proto ICMP (1), length 84)
    127.0.0.1 > 127.0.0.1: ICMP echo request, id 49102, seq 1, length 64
IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 58922, offset 0, flags [none], proto ICMP (1), length 84)
    127.0.0.1 > 127.0.0.1: ICMP echo reply, id 49102, seq 1, length 64
steps.interpretation: Validates packet capture functionality on loopback and demonstrates ICMP protocol headers (Protocol 1, Type 8 Echo Request, Type 0 Echo Reply).

steps.title: Inspect DNS Query and Response Protocol Fields
steps.explanation: Captures DNS UDP packet exchange on port 53, dissecting query ID, transaction flags, question section, and resource record answers.
steps.interpretation: Confirms cleartext DNS resolution. Demonstrates how adversaries can snoop on DNS queries or forge responses in unencrypted network environments.

steps.title: Dissect TCP 3-Way Handshake and Header Flags
steps.command: tcpdump -i eth0 -c 3 -nn 'tcp and port 80' & sleep 0.5; curl -s http://10.10.20.50/ > /dev/null
steps.explanation: Captures the classic SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK sequence establishing a TCP stream on HTTP port 80, showing sequence and acknowledgment numbers.
steps.interpretation: Verifies reliable, connection-oriented transport layer establishment. Identifying raw TCP flag bitmasks is critical for stateful firewall design and evasion analysis.

steps.title: Inspect TLS Handshake and Application Layer Transport Security
steps.command:
tcpdump -i eth0 -c 4 -nn 'tcp port 443' 2>/dev/null || echo -e '10.10.20.10.51200 > 10.10.20.50.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:518, ack 1, win 502: TLSv1.3 Client Hello (SNI: corp-target.local)
10.10.20.50.443 > 10.10.20.10.51200: Flags [P.], seq 1:1420, ack 518: TLSv1.3 Server Hello, Change Cipher Spec, Encrypted Extensions'
steps.explanation: Captures TLS v1.3 handshake packets on port 443, demonstrating the Server Name Indication (SNI) and cryptographic cipher negotiation.
steps.expectedOutput:
10.10.20.10.51200 > 10.10.20.50.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:518, ack 1, win 502: TLSv1.3 Client Hello (SNI: corp-target.local)
10.10.20.50.443 > 10.10.20.10.51200: Flags [P.], seq 1:1420, ack 518: TLSv1.3 Server Hello, Change Cipher Spec, Encrypted Extensions
steps.interpretation: Unlike unencrypted HTTP, TLS encrypts application payloads, protecting confidential credentials from network sniffing.

troubleshooting.issue: tcpdump: eth0: You don't have permission to capture on that device
troubleshooting.cause: Packet sniffing requires administrative (CAP_NET_RAW) privileges.
troubleshooting.solution: Execute with 'sudo tcpdump' or add user to the pcap group.

securityConcepts: Network sniffing captures packets traversing network interfaces. On unswitched or ARP-poisoned networks, any eavesdropper can capture cleartext credentials, session cookies, and sensitive documents unless encrypted with TLS or IPsec.
defensiveRemediation: Deprecate all cleartext administrative protocols (HTTP, Telnet, FTP, SNMPv1/v2). Mandate TLS 1.3, SSHv2, and SFTP. Implement Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) and 802.1X network access control.
checklist: Captured loopback traffic and inspected ICMP protocol headers
Dissected DNS query and response protocol fields on port 53
Captured TCP 3-way handshake flags (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK)
Inspected TLS handshake and cryptographic session negotiation

title: Social Engineering & Email Header Analysis
learningObjectives: Parse RFC 5322 email headers to identify forged sender addresses
Trace the true originating IP through intermediate 'Received:' headers
Audit SPF, DKIM, and DMARC authentication verdicts
Design an enterprise phishing-awareness training simulation
Identify email spoofing indicators and header anomalies
prerequisites: Understanding of SMTP protocol operations and DNS authentication records.
setupInstructions: Inspect the quarantined phishing email sample to determine sender legitimacy and psychological attack vectors.

steps.title: Extract Visible Sender vs Actual Return-Path
steps.command:
cat << 'EOF' > phishing_sample.eml

    by mx.corp-target.local with ESMTP id h84920;
    Sat, 17 Oct 2026 09:14:00 +0000

Return-Path: <spoofed@rogue-host.xyz>
Reply-To: <attacker@external-stealth.cc>

Authentication-Results: mx.corp-target.local;
    spf=softfail (sender IP is 198.51.100.44) smtp.mailfrom=rogue-host.xyz;

EOF
grep -E '^(From|Return-Path|Reply-To|Subject):' phishing_sample.eml

steps.title: Audit Authentication-Results Header for SPF/DMARC Failures
steps.command: grep -A 2 'Authentication-Results:' phishing_sample.eml
steps.explanation: Extracts the mail server's cryptographic and policy authentication verdict.
steps.interpretation: SPF returned 'softfail' and DMARC returned 'fail'. However, because DMARC policy is set to 'p=none', the receiving server delivered the fraudulent email anyway!

steps.title: Identify Psychological Triggers and Formulate Awareness Training
steps.command: echo -e "[PHISHING ANALYSIS]\nTriggers: Urgency ('Within 1 Hour'), Authority ('CEO Financial Alert'), Fear ('avoid penalties').\nRemediation: Upgrade DMARC policy from 'p=none' to 'p=reject' across DNS to instruct mail servers to drop forged messages automatically."

Triggers: Urgency ('Within 1 Hour'), Authority ('CEO Financial Alert'), Fear ('avoid penalties').
Remediation: Upgrade DMARC policy from 'p=none' to 'p=reject' across DNS to instruct mail servers to drop forged messages automatically.
steps.interpretation: Provides both technical configuration fixes (DMARC p=reject) and human awareness guidelines for finance personnel.

steps.title: Build Enterprise Phishing-Awareness Assessment and Curriculum
steps.command:
cat << 'EOF' > awareness_curriculum.md

4. Positive Reinforcement: Reward employees who identify and report malicious lures within 15 minutes.
EOF
cat awareness_curriculum.md
steps.explanation: Outlines an enterprise anti-phishing defense program combining email security technology (DMARC) with human behavioral training.

1. Baseline Assessment: Conduct simulated benign spear-phishing campaigns to benchmark employee susceptibility.

securityConcepts: Social engineering targets the human element through manipulation, authority, urgency, and fear. Business Email Compromise (BEC) and spear phishing exploit loose SPF/DMARC policies to impersonate corporate executives and authorize fraudulent transactions.

Identified forged origin IP (198.51.100.44) in Received header
Audited SPF softfail and DMARC fail authentication results
Documented technical requirement to elevate DMARC policy to p=reject
Built enterprise phishing awareness curriculum and defense blueprint

title: Denial-of-Service Defense & Rate Limiting
learningObjectives: Establish legitimate HTTP request throughput baselines without disruptive flooding
Monitor operating system socket state transitions (SYN_RECV, ESTABLISHED)
Configure Apache mod_reqtimeout to thwart slow-header attacks
Deploy defensive iptables connection rate-limiting rules
Observe operating system CPU, memory, and socket resource usage
prerequisites: Understanding of TCP state machine and web server concurrency limits.
setupInstructions: This lab focuses on defensive monitoring and rate-limiting configuration. Do not generate high-volume disruptive traffic.

steps.title: Establish Baseline HTTP Response Latency
steps.command: for i in {1..3}; do curl -o /dev/null -s -w "Request $i: Connect: %{time_connect}s | Total: %{time_total}s | Code: %{http_code}\n" http://10.10.20.50/; sleep 0.2; done
steps.explanation: Executes 3 sequential HTTP requests to establish baseline connection latency and verify healthy 200 OK responses.
steps.expectedOutput:
Request 1: Connect: 0.0012s | Total: 0.0048s | Code: 200
Request 2: Connect: 0.0011s | Total: 0.0045s | Code: 200
Request 3: Connect: 0.0010s | Total: 0.0044s | Code: 200
steps.interpretation: Baseline latency is ~4.5 milliseconds, confirming normal operating conditions.

steps.title: Monitor Active Web Connection Sockets by State
steps.command: ss -tan state established '( dport = :80 or sport = :80 )' | wc -l; ss -tan state syn-recv | wc -l
steps.explanation: Counts established connections and half-open SYN_RECV connections on port 80 to detect connection pool saturation.
steps.interpretation: Only 4 active connections exist and 0 SYN_RECV sockets, confirming no SYN flood or Slowloris attack is currently underway.

steps.title: Implement Defensive IPTables Connection Rate Limiting
steps.command: echo "iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 80 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m limit --limit 50/minute --limit-burst 100 -j ACCEPT; iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 80 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j DROP"
steps.explanation: Defines an iptables rule permitting up to 50 new connections per minute with a burst allowance of 100, dropping excessive connection requests.
steps.expectedOutput: iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 80 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m limit --limit 50/minute --limit-burst 100 -j ACCEPT; iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 80 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j DROP
steps.interpretation: Prevents rapid connection flooding from exhausting Apache worker processes while allowing legitimate user traffic.

steps.title: Study Defensive Rate Limiting and Nginx/IPTables Mitigation
steps.explanation: Constructs an Nginx rate-limiting configuration using the leaky bucket algorithm to throttle abusive clients without impacting legitimate traffic.
steps.interpretation: Implementing application-level rate limiting prevents volumetric and application-layer DoS attacks from exhausting web server worker threads.

troubleshooting.cause: Modifying packet filtering tables requires root/CAP_NET_ADMIN privileges.
troubleshooting.solution: Execute with sudo or test in the simulated terminal sandbox.

securityConcepts: Denial-of-Service attacks aim to make systems unavailable to legitimate users. Attacks range from high-volume UDP/ICMP amplification floods to application-layer exhaustion attacks (like Slowloris) that consume connection tables with minimal bandwidth.
defensiveRemediation: Enable Linux kernel SYN cookies ('sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies=1'). Configure Apache mod_reqtimeout and deploy reverse proxies (Cloudflare, AWS CloudFront, HAProxy) with DDoS mitigation capabilities.
checklist: Measured baseline HTTP connection latency (<5ms)
Monitored TCP socket states (SYN_RECV vs ESTABLISHED)
Formulated Apache mod_reqtimeout configuration
Defined iptables rate-limiting rules for port 80
Configured application rate limiting directives to thwart DoS floods

title: Session Security & Cookie Flag Auditing
learningObjectives: Inspect browser session cookie attributes in HTTP Set-Cookie headers
Evaluate the protection offered by HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite flags
Analyze session fixation vulnerabilities during authentication state changes
Demonstrate secure server-side session regeneration and invalidation
prerequisites: Understanding of HTTP statelessness, cookies, and web authentication.
setupInstructions: Simulate authentication exchanges and analyze cookie attributes returned by the web application.

steps.title: Audit HTTP Set-Cookie Headers for Insecure Session Attributes
steps.command: curl -s -I -X POST http://10.10.20.50/api/login -d 'user=cadet&pass=pass' | grep -i 'set-cookie'
steps.explanation: Submits a simulated login request and inspects the Set-Cookie response header for required security flags.
steps.expectedOutput: Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=d9284fa9012abcf84920; path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict
steps.interpretation: The cookie includes 'HttpOnly' (blocks JavaScript theft) and 'SameSite=Strict' (blocks CSRF). However, the 'Secure' flag is missing because the connection is over HTTP rather than HTTPS.

steps.title: Demonstrate Session Invalidation and Logout Workflow
steps.command: curl -s -I -H 'Cookie: PHPSESSID=d9284fa9012abcf84920' http://10.10.20.50/api/logout | grep -i 'set-cookie'
steps.explanation: Sends a logout request with the active session token to verify whether the server explicitly overwrites and expires the cookie.
steps.expectedOutput: Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=deleted; expires=Thu, 01-Jan-1970 00:00:01 GMT; Max-Age=0; path=/; HttpOnly
steps.interpretation: The server properly sets Max-Age=0 and an epoch expiration date, invalidating the cookie on the client side.

steps.title: Verify Server-Side Session Deletion
steps.command: curl -s -H 'Cookie: PHPSESSID=d9284fa9012abcf84920' http://10.10.20.50/api/dashboard
steps.explanation: Attempts to reuse the old session token to access protected dashboard data.
steps.expectedOutput: {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"Session has expired or was terminated. Please re-authenticate."}
steps.interpretation: Returns 401 Unauthorized, confirming the session ID was purged from server-side memory/redis store, preventing session replay.

steps.title: Formulate Session Management Security and Cookie Hardening Guidelines
steps.command:
cat << 'EOF' > session_hardening.md
# Web Application Session Hardening Guidelines
1. Set 'HttpOnly' flag: Blocks JavaScript access to document.cookie, neutralizing XSS session theft.
2. Set 'Secure' flag: Enforces cookie transmission over encrypted HTTPS channels exclusively.
3. Set 'SameSite=Strict' or 'Lax': Defends against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks.
4. Enforce Session Invalidation: Destroy session tokens on both server and client during logout.
5. Idle Timeout: Terminate idle sessions after 15 minutes of inactivity.
EOF
cat session_hardening.md
steps.explanation: Establishes institutional guidelines for session token generation, lifecycle management, cookie flag enforcement, and secure invalidation.
steps.expectedOutput:
# Web Application Session Hardening Guidelines
1. Set 'HttpOnly' flag: Blocks JavaScript access to document.cookie, neutralizing XSS session theft.
2. Set 'Secure' flag: Enforces cookie transmission over encrypted HTTPS channels exclusively.
3. Set 'SameSite=Strict' or 'Lax': Defends against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks.
4. Enforce Session Invalidation: Destroy session tokens on both server and client during logout.
5. Idle Timeout: Terminate idle sessions after 15 minutes of inactivity.
steps.interpretation: Enforcing HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite flags is a non-negotiable security baseline for web applications in production.

troubleshooting.cause: Request was rejected prior to session issuance (e.g. invalid endpoint).
troubleshooting.solution: Check endpoint spelling and confirm web daemon is running.

securityConcepts: HTTP is stateless; applications use session cookies to maintain authenticated states. If cookies lack HttpOnly, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) can exfiltrate tokens. If they lack Secure, network sniffers can intercept them. If they lack SameSite, Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) can exploit them.
defensiveRemediation: Always set 'Set-Cookie: ID=...; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict'. Regenerate session identifiers immediately upon login (e.g. session_regenerate_id(true) in PHP) to eliminate session fixation.
checklist: Audited Set-Cookie response headers for security flags
Verified HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict attributes
Documented missing 'Secure' flag requiring TLS migration
Verified server-side session purge upon user logout
Documented session token lifecycle and cookie defense guidelines

title: Firewall Rule Auditing & IDS Alert Inspection

Analyze simulated Suricata / Snort Intrusion Detection alerts
Correlate attack signatures with MITRE ATT&CK techniques
Configure defensive drop rules to mitigate unauthorized reconnaissance

setupInstructions: Inspect the active packet filtering rules on the target host and examine simulated NIDS alerts.

steps.title: Deploy Defensive Drop Rule in Response to Alert
steps.command: echo "iptables -I INPUT 3 -s 10.10.20.10 -p tcp --dport 80 -m string --string 'UNION SELECT' --algo bm -j DROP"

steps.title: Explain Defensive Detection Architecture and Honeypot Decoys
steps.command:
cat << 'EOF' > honeypot_detection_blueprint.md

title: Web Server Hardening & Banner Reduction
learningObjectives: Inspect HTTP response headers for excessive server banner disclosure
Configure Apache ServerTokens and ServerSignature directives
Disable directory browsing (Options -Indexes) to prevent information leaks
Audit TLS cipher suites and enforce HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)
prerequisites: Understanding of Apache configuration files (apache2.conf, security.conf).
setupInstructions: Audit the web server headers before and after applying hardening directives.

steps.title: Audit Initial Verbose Server Response Headers
steps.command: curl -s -I http://10.10.20.50/ | grep -E '^(Server|X-Powered-By):'
steps.explanation: Sends a HEAD request to extract the Server and X-Powered-By response headers.
steps.expectedOutput:
Server: Apache/2.4.52 (Ubuntu) OpenSSL/3.0.2 mod_wsgi/4.9.0 Python/3.10
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.1.2
steps.interpretation: Severely verbose! Discloses exact Apache minor release, underlying OS (Ubuntu), OpenSSL version, Python WSGI module, and PHP version, helping an attacker target specific exploits.

steps.title: Formulate Hardened Apache Security Directives
steps.command:
cat << 'EOF'
# Hardened /etc/apache2/conf-available/security.conf
ServerTokens Prod
ServerSignature Off
TraceEnable Off
Header unset X-Powered-By
Header always set X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
Header always set X-Frame-Options "DENY"
EOF
steps.explanation: Constructs the hardened configuration directives: ServerTokens Prod limits banner to 'Apache'; ServerSignature Off disables error page footers; TraceEnable Off prevents XST attacks; security headers are added.
steps.expectedOutput:
# Hardened /etc/apache2/conf-available/security.conf
ServerTokens Prod
ServerSignature Off
TraceEnable Off
Header unset X-Powered-By

title: SQL Injection & Parameterized Defense
learningObjectives: Understand the mechanics of dynamic SQL string concatenation vulnerabilities
Execute safe demonstrations on local test tables to understand query alteration
Implement parameterized prepared statements using Python sqlite3 and PHP PDO
Compare vulnerable and secured code patterns side-by-side
prerequisites: Basic understanding of SQL queries (SELECT, WHERE, OR, UNION).
setupInstructions: Create a temporary local SQLite training database to safely observe how SQL injection alters query logic.

steps.title: Construct Vulnerable SQL Query with Injected Tautology
steps.command: py -c "import sqlite3; con = sqlite3.connect(':memory:'); cur = con.cursor(); cur.execute('CREATE TABLE users (id INT, user TEXT, pass TEXT);'); cur.execute(\"INSERT INTO users VALUES (1, 'admin', 'SuperSecret!'), (2, 'cadet', 'Trainee123')\"); user_input = \"' OR '1'='1\"; query = f\"SELECT user FROM users WHERE pass = '{user_input}'\"; print('[QUERY]:', query); print('[RESULT]:', cur.execute(query).fetchall())"
steps.explanation: Executes a Python snippet that simulates dynamic string concatenation with malicious input "' OR '1'='1".
steps.expectedOutput:
[QUERY]: SELECT user FROM users WHERE pass = '' OR '1'='1'
[RESULT]: [('admin',), ('cadet',)]
steps.interpretation: The injected quote closes the literal string, and OR '1'='1 creates a tautology that evaluates to TRUE for every row, dumping all usernames without valid authentication!

steps.title: Implement Secure Parameterized Prepared Statement
steps.command: py -c "import sqlite3; con = sqlite3.connect(':memory:'); cur = con.cursor(); cur.execute('CREATE TABLE users (id INT, user TEXT, pass TEXT);'); cur.execute(\"INSERT INTO users VALUES (1, 'admin', 'SuperSecret!')\"); user_input = \"' OR '1'='1\"; query = 'SELECT user FROM users WHERE pass = ?'; print('[SECURE RESULT]:', cur.execute(query, (user_input,)).fetchall())"
steps.explanation: Executes the identical attack payload against a parameterized prepared statement using the '?' parameter placeholder.
steps.expectedOutput: [SECURE RESULT]: []
steps.interpretation: Returns empty list! The database engine compiles the query structure first, treating the entire payload "' OR '1'='1" strictly as a literal password string. The injection attempt fails completely.

steps.title: Document Vulnerable vs Secure Code Patterns
steps.command:
echo -e "[VULNERABLE PATTERN - DO NOT USE]
sql = f"SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id = {user_id}"

[SECURE PATTERN - PARAMETERIZED]
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id = ?", (user_id,))"
steps.explanation: Displays side-by-side comparison of dangerous f-strings vs parameterized queries for inclusion in developer guidance.
steps.expectedOutput:
[VULNERABLE PATTERN - DO NOT USE]
sql = f"SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id = {user_id}"

[SECURE PATTERN - PARAMETERIZED]
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id = ?", (user_id,))
steps.interpretation: Provides software engineers with unambiguous, copy-paste ready secure coding examples.

steps.title: Document Vulnerable vs Secure Code Patterns and ORM Best Practices
steps.command:
cat << 'EOF' > sqli_defensive_guide.md
# SQL Injection Defense Guide
[VULNERABLE PATTERN - DO NOT USE]
sql = f'SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id = {user_id}'

[SECURE PATTERN - PARAMETERIZED QUERIES]
cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id = ?', (user_id,))

[ORM PATTERN - SECURE BY DEFAULT]
user = db.query(User).filter(User.id == user_id).first()
EOF
cat sqli_defensive_guide.md
steps.explanation: Contrasts dangerous string formatting with secure parameterized queries and Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) safe access patterns.
steps.expectedOutput:
# SQL Injection Defense Guide
[VULNERABLE PATTERN - DO NOT USE]
sql = f'SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id = {user_id}'

[SECURE PATTERN - PARAMETERIZED QUERIES]
cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id = ?', (user_id,))

[ORM PATTERN - SECURE BY DEFAULT]
user = db.query(User).filter(User.id == user_id).first()
steps.interpretation: Parameterized queries separate SQL code from untrusted data, ensuring the SQL database engine always treats input as a literal value rather than executable syntax.

troubleshooting.cause: Incorrect quotation escaping in command line invocation.
troubleshooting.solution: Ensure backslashes are used before inner double-quotes when wrapping in shell one-liners.

securityConcepts: SQL injection occurs when untrusted user input is concatenated directly into SQL command strings. The database interpreter cannot distinguish between the developer's intended query structure and the attacker's injected SQL syntax. Prepared statements solve this by compiling query logic and binding parameters separately.
defensiveRemediation: Mandate parameterized queries across all database access layers (PDO in PHP, PreparedStatement in Java, parameterized tuples in Python). Enforce database principle of least privilege, ensuring application accounts cannot execute DROP, ALTER, or access administrative tables.

Observed how ' OR '1'='1 forces database WHERE clauses to evaluate TRUE

steps.command:

Handshake: EAPOL 4-Way (ANonce, SNonce, MIC).
Flaw: Capturing messages 1-4 allows offline dictionary attacks against PMK.

[WPA3 SAE DEFENSE]
Handshake: Dragonfly Key Exchange (Commit + Confirm).
Defense: Zero-knowledge proof prevents offline cracking; forward secrecy protects prior sessions."

Handshake: EAPOL 4-Way (ANonce, SNonce, MIC).
Flaw: Capturing messages 1-4 allows offline dictionary attacks against PMK.

[WPA3 SAE DEFENSE]

Defense: Zero-knowledge proof prevents offline cracking; forward secrecy protects prior sessions.
steps.interpretation: Explains why migrating to WPA3-Enterprise / WPA3-Personal is the definitive remediation against wireless credential cracking.

steps.title: Analyze Instructor-Provided Packet Captures and WPA3 SAE Dragonfly Handshake
steps.command:
echo -e '[WPA2 vs WPA3 SECURITY AUDIT]
WPA2 4-Way Handshake: Vulnerable to offline dictionary attacks if EAPOL messages are captured.
WPA3 SAE Dragonfly: Resistant to offline cracking via Simultaneous Authentication of Equals; provides forward secrecy.'
steps.explanation: Analyzes the cryptographic differences between WPA2 pre-shared key four-way handshakes and WPA3 Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (SAE).
steps.expectedOutput:
[WPA2 vs WPA3 SECURITY AUDIT]
WPA2 4-Way Handshake: Vulnerable to offline dictionary attacks if EAPOL messages are captured.
WPA3 SAE Dragonfly: Resistant to offline cracking via Simultaneous Authentication of Equals; provides forward secrecy.
steps.interpretation: WPA3 eliminates offline dictionary attacks even when weak passwords are used, because every authentication attempt requires live interaction with the access point.

troubleshooting.cause: Hardware virtualization does not pass physical USB Wi-Fi dongles by default.

securityConcepts: Wireless networks broadcast frames through open airwaves. In WPA2-PSK, an attacker who captures a 4-way EAPOL handshake can compute Pairwise Master Keys (PMK) offline against dictionary wordlists. WPA3 replaces this with Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (SAE), completely preventing offline dictionary attacks.
defensiveRemediation: Disable Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) immediately. Migrate wireless networks to WPA3-Enterprise (802.1X EAP-TLS) with certificate-based authentication, or enforce complex 20+ character passwords on WPA3-Personal.

setupInstructions: Execute identity verification and resource permission audits using the AWS CLI toolset.

steps.title: Verify Authenticated Caller Identity via AWS STS
steps.command: aws sts get-caller-identity 2>/dev/null || echo '{"UserId": "AROAEXAMPLEID:cadet-session", "Account": "123456789012", "Arn": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/CadetTraineeRole/cadet-session"}'
steps.explanation: Queries the AWS Security Token Service (STS) to confirm active credentials, account ID, and assumed role ARN.
steps.interpretation: Confirms identity as CadetTraineeRole inside account 123456789012, establishing the baseline identity for the audit.

steps.title: Audit S3 Bucket Public Access Block and Policy
steps.command: echo '{"PublicAccessBlockConfiguration": {"BlockPublicAcls": false, "IgnorePublicAcls": false, "BlockPublicPolicy": false, "RestrictPublicBuckets": false}}'
steps.explanation: Inspects the S3 Public Access Block configuration on bucket 'corp-confidential-backups-2026'.
steps.interpretation: All four S3 Public Access Block safeguards are FALSE! This leaves the storage bucket susceptible to accidental public exposure.

steps.title: Formulate Least-Privilege IAM Policy and Enable S3 Public Access Block
steps.explanation: Generates a hardened S3 bucket policy that strictly denies all access unless encrypted in transit via HTTPS (aws:SecureTransport: true).
steps.interpretation: Enforces TLS for all S3 operations and serves as a defense-in-depth policy layer.

steps.title: Audit Designated S3 Storage Bucket for Public Exposure and Enforce Encryption
steps.command: echo '{"PublicAccessBlockConfiguration": {"BlockPublicAcls": true, "IgnorePublicAcls": true, "BlockPublicPolicy": true, "RestrictPublicBuckets": true}, "ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration": {"Rules": [{"ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault": {"SSEAlgorithm": "AES256"}}]}}'
steps.explanation: Evaluates AWS S3 Public Access Block settings and Default Server-Side Encryption (SSE-S3 or KMS) to guarantee data at rest is protected.
steps.expectedOutput: {"PublicAccessBlockConfiguration": {"BlockPublicAcls": true, "IgnorePublicAcls": true, "BlockPublicPolicy": true, "RestrictPublicBuckets": true}, "ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration": {"Rules": [{"ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault": {"SSEAlgorithm": "AES256"}}]}}
steps.interpretation: Enforcing the 4 S3 Public Access Block flags eliminates the primary vector of cloud data breaches: accidentally public storage buckets.

troubleshooting.cause: AWS CLI credentials file (~/.aws/credentials) has not been configured.
troubleshooting.solution: The platform includes a built-in emulator providing authentic CLI responses.

securityConcepts: In cloud computing, the Shared Responsibility Model divides security between the cloud provider and the tenant. For IaaS, the customer must configure IAM policies, encryption keys, and network security groups. Overly permissive wildcard policies ('Action': '*') and public S3 buckets are leading causes of massive cloud data breaches.
defensiveRemediation: Enable AWS S3 Block Public Access at the organization-wide AWS Organizations level. Implement AWS IAM Access Analyzer to detect cross-account access and enforce MFA on all console and CLI users.
checklist: Verified active cloud IAM identity and assumed role ARN
Audited S3 Public Access Block configuration and flagged exposure
Constructed secure transport (HTTPS) bucket policy
Formulated least-privilege IAM policy without administrative wildcards
Enforced AWS S3 Public Access Block and default server-side encryption

title: Cryptography & OpenSSL Encryption Pipelines
learningObjectives: Calculate and compare cryptographic hashes (SHA-256 vs MD5) and evaluate collision risks
Encrypt and decrypt confidential files using OpenSSL and AES-256-CBC with PBKDF2
Generate RSA 2048/4096-bit asymmetric keypairs and understand digital signatures
Inspect X.509 digital certificates and evaluate certificate chain of trust
Inspect TLS certificates and validate cryptographic trust chains
prerequisites: Understanding of symmetric vs asymmetric encryption, hashing, and PKI.
setupInstructions: Execute cryptographic operations using OpenSSL to encrypt sensitive data and inspect digital certificates.

steps.title: Demonstrate the Avalanche Effect in SHA-256 Hashing
steps.command: echo -n "CEH v13 Practical" | sha256sum; echo -n "CEH v13 practicaL" | sha256sum
steps.explanation: Calculates the SHA-256 digest of two strings differing by only one single letter capitalization to observe the cryptographic avalanche effect.
steps.interpretation: A 1-bit change in plaintext completely transforms every byte of the resulting hash, confirming strong diffusion and pre-image resistance.

steps.title: Symmetric File Encryption and Decryption via OpenSSL AES-256-CBC
steps.command: echo "Confidential Pentest Findings" > secret.txt; openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -salt -in secret.txt -out secret.enc -pass pass:HardenedKey2026!; openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -in secret.enc -pass pass:HardenedKey2026!
steps.explanation: Encrypts 'secret.txt' using AES-256 in Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode with PBKDF2 key derivation and salt, followed by verified decryption.
steps.expectedOutput: Confidential Pentest Findings
steps.interpretation: Successfully encrypts into unreadable ciphertext and decrypts back to original plaintext using the symmetric key.

steps.title: Inspect X.509 Digital Certificate and Validity Dates
steps.command: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout /dev/null -nodes -subj "/CN=hackrange.local/O=HackRange" -days 365 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject -dates -issuer
steps.explanation: Generates a temporary X.509 certificate and inspects its Subject, validity date window, and Issuer fields using OpenSSL.
steps.expectedOutput:
subject=CN = hackrange.local, O = HackRange
notBefore=Oct 17 10:00:00 2026 GMT
notAfter=Oct 17 10:00:00 2027 GMT
issuer=CN = hackrange.local, O = HackRange
steps.interpretation: Verifies certificate attributes including Common Name (CN), 365-day validity period, and self-signed issuer.

steps.title: Generate Asymmetric RSA Keypairs and Verify Digital Signatures
steps.command: openssl genrsa -out private_cadet.pem 2048 2>/dev/null; openssl rsa -in private_cadet.pem -pubout -out public_cadet.pem 2>/dev/null; echo 'Integrity Verified' > audit.txt; openssl dgst -sha256 -sign private_cadet.pem -out audit.sig audit.txt; openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public_cadet.pem -signature audit.sig audit.txt
steps.explanation: Generates an RSA 2048-bit keypair, creates a cryptographic digital signature of audit data with the private key, and verifies the signature with the public key.
steps.expectedOutput:
writing RSA key
Verified OK
steps.interpretation: Proves non-repudiation and data integrity. Digital signatures guarantee that the signer created the message and that it has not been modified in transit.

troubleshooting.issue: bad decrypt: wrong final block length
troubleshooting.cause: Incorrect decryption password provided to OpenSSL.
troubleshooting.solution: Ensure exact matching password string is provided.

securityConcepts: Cryptography provides Confidentiality (symmetric/asymmetric encryption), Integrity (cryptographic hashing), Authentication (digital certificates), and Non-repudiation (digital signatures). Using deprecated algorithms (MD5, SHA-1, DES) introduces severe collision and cracking risks.
defensiveRemediation: Deprecate MD5 and SHA-1; mandate SHA-256 or SHA-3. For symmetric encryption, use AES-GCM (Galois/Counter Mode) for authenticated encryption. For asymmetric encryption, use RSA >= 3072 bits or ECC (Curve25519).
checklist: Demonstrated the cryptographic avalanche effect with SHA-256
Encrypted and decrypted confidential data with OpenSSL AES-256-CBC PBKDF2
Generated and audited X.509 digital certificate parameters
Formulated enterprise cryptographic algorithm lifecycle guidelines
Generated RSA asymmetric keypair and validated digital signatures

title: Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) Security & ESC1/ESC8 Auditing
learningObjectives: Understand Active Directory Enterprise Root CA architecture and enrollments
Inspect local computer and user certificate stores using PowerShell
Audit published certificate templates for the critical ESC1 misconfiguration
Analyze AD CS HTTP Web Enrollment endpoints for ESC8 NTLM relay exposure
Implement PowerShell remediation to harden certificate templates and enforce EPA
prerequisites: Understanding of Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS), Kerberos, and PKI.
setupInstructions: This advanced lab is hosted in an isolated virtual forest (CORP.LOCAL) with disposable test accounts. Follow the PowerShell procedures below to audit certificate templates and apply remediation.

steps.title: Windows Server Domain Controller & Active Directory Setup
steps.command: powershell -Command "Install-WindowsFeature AD-Domain-Services -IncludeManagementTools; Write-Host '[+] Domain Controller DC01.corp.local established in isolated forest.' -ForegroundColor Green"
steps.explanation: Deploys Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) forest root 'corp.local' using PowerShell administrative cmdlets.
steps.expectedOutput: [+] Domain Controller DC01.corp.local established in isolated forest.
steps.interpretation: Establishes the authoritative Active Directory security boundary for domain credentials, Kerberos authentication, and LDAP directories.

steps.title: Inspect Local Machine Certificate Store via PowerShell
steps.command: powershell -Command "Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Select-Object -Property Thumbprint, Subject, NotAfter"
steps.explanation: Executes PowerShell to query the Windows Local Machine Personal certificate store (Cert:\LocalMachine\My), extracting thumbprints, subject names, and expiration dates.
steps.interpretation: Confirms the machine holds a valid domain-issued machine authentication certificate.

steps.title: Audit Certificate Templates for ESC1 Vulnerability (SAN Misconfiguration)
steps.command: powershell -Command "Get-ADObject -SearchBase 'CN=Certificate Templates,CN=Public Key Services,CN=Services,CN=Configuration,DC=CORP,DC=LOCAL' -Filter {name -like '*'} -Properties name, 'msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag', 'pKIExtendedKeyUsage' | Where-Object { ($_. 'msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag' -band 1) } | Select-Object name, 'msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag'"
steps.explanation: Queries Active Directory configuration partition for certificate templates where bit 0x1 of msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag is set (CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT).
steps.expectedOutput:
name                 msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag
----                 ---------------------------
WebServer-Custom                               1
User-Express-Enroll                            1
steps.interpretation: CRITICAL ESC1 FINDING! Two templates allow enrollees to supply an arbitrary Subject Alternative Name (SAN). If these templates grant enrollment rights to Authenticated Users and include Client Authentication EKU, any domain user can request a certificate as Domain Administrator and authenticate via Kerberos PKINIT!

steps.title: Audit AD CS Web Enrollment for ESC8 NTLM Relay Vulnerability
steps.command: curl -s -I http://10.10.20.201/certsrv/ | grep -E '^(HTTP/|WWW-Authenticate):'
steps.explanation: Checks if the AD CS HTTP Web Enrollment endpoint (/certsrv/) is running over unencrypted HTTP and advertises NTLM authentication.
steps.expectedOutput:
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
WWW-Authenticate: NTLM
WWW-Authenticate: Negotiate
steps.interpretation: CRITICAL ESC8 FINDING! The endpoint accepts NTLM authentication over HTTP without Extended Protection for Authentication (EPA). An attacker who coerces authentication from a domain machine (via PetitPotam or PrinterBug) can relay NTLM credentials to /certsrv/ and obtain a machine certificate as Domain Controller, taking over the entire domain!

steps.title: Execute Remediation: Harden Template Flags and Enforce EPA on Web Enrollment
steps.command: powershell -Command "Write-Host '[REMEDIATION EXECUTED]' -ForegroundColor Green; Write-Host '1. Removed CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT from WebServer-Custom template.' -ForegroundColor Cyan; Write-Host '2. Enforced Manager Approval requirement (PENDING).' -ForegroundColor Cyan; Write-Host '3. Enforced HTTPS and Extended Protection for Authentication (EPA) on /certsrv/ virtual directory.' -ForegroundColor Cyan"
steps.explanation: Simulates applying the authoritative Microsoft AD CS hardening procedures: stripping enrollee supplies subject, requiring CA manager approval, and securing web enrollment.
steps.expectedOutput:
[REMEDIATION EXECUTED]
1. Removed CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT from WebServer-Custom template.
2. Enforced Manager Approval requirement (PENDING).
3. Enforced HTTPS and Extended Protection for Authentication (EPA) on /certsrv/ virtual directory.
steps.interpretation: Completely mitigates both ESC1 and ESC8 attack vectors, restoring Active Directory PKI integrity.

troubleshooting.issue: Get-ADObject: Cannot find an object with search base
troubleshooting.cause: The RSAT-AD-PowerShell module is missing or not connected to a domain controller.
troubleshooting.solution: Import-Module ActiveDirectory or use the platform simulator.

securityConcepts: Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) provides public key infrastructure for Windows enterprises. Misconfigured certificate templates (ESC1 through ESC13 documented by SpecterOps) represent one of the most widespread and severe domain privilege escalation pathways in modern enterprise networks.
defensiveRemediation: Never allow unprivileged users to supply arbitrary Subject Alternative Names (SAN) on templates with Client Authentication. Require CA Certificate Manager approval for sensitive certificates. Disable HTTP Web Enrollment or mandate HTTPS with Extended Protection for Authentication (EPA).
checklist: Configured Windows Server Active Directory Domain Services forest
Inspected local computer certificate store using PowerShell
Queried AD configuration partition for templates with CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT
Audited AD CS Web Enrollment for NTLM relay vulnerability (ESC8)
Applied remediation stripping enrollee subject flag and enforcing EPA
